title: Epic: Kernel auto-selection v2 (model family + seq regime + GPU SKU) with safe rollout and observability
creator: Talia Benson
project: Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel auto-selection v2
description:
Goal
Ship kernel auto-selection v2 in Serving Runtime to reduce p95/p99 latency and improve throughput stability across heterogeneous GPU fleets (A100/H100/L40S) while preserving correctness + determinism guarantees and enabling rapid rollback / customer overrides.

What’s changing (v1 -> v2)
- v1 selection is mostly static per-model defaults with limited GPU awareness; v2 makes selection decisions keyed on:
  1) model family / architecture tags (e.g., Llama/Mistral/Qwen/Gemma)
  2) sequence length regime (prefill/decode characteristics; short vs long context; mixed workloads)
  3) GPU type / SKU (normalized naming; MIG-aware where applicable)
- v2 introduces explicit fallback hierarchy when kernels are missing/unstable and adds selection telemetry to make decisions explainable and replayable.

Scope
- Runtime selector module: feature extraction, candidate generation, scoring/decision rules, fallbacks
- GPU-SKU keyed kernel registry + denylist plumbing for known-bad kernel/SKU/driver combos
- Determinism + replay tests (same inputs => same selection), plus guardrails against long-context misclassification
- Observability: per-request selection events with sampling, dashboards for rollout monitoring
- Perf suite expansion: long-context + mixed workloads across model families + GPU SKUs; pass/fail thresholds
- Rollout mechanics: feature gate + per-model allowlist/denylist, staged region rollout, rapid rollback path
- Documentation/runbooks for oncall + Dedicated/Private overrides

Out of scope
- Learned model for kernel selection (ADR chooses rule-based for explainability/rollback)
- New kernels themselves beyond mapping/selection (kernel implementations tracked separately)

Success metrics (GA gates)
- Correctness: zero known correctness regressions; deterministic selection verified in CI and spot-checked in prod replay
- Perf: no p95 regression > 1% and no p99 regression > 2% on covered canary scenarios; targeted improvements on at least 60% of high-volume routes (see benchmark matrix)
- Stability: reduction in p99 volatility for mixed workloads (scheduler-integrated hints enabled)
- Ops: dashboards live + alerting tuned; rollback tested; oncall runbook validated during canary

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Discovery + design
- Design doc + ADR
- Finalize feature set, rule ordering, fallback hierarchy, determinism requirements

2) Implementation behind gates
- Land v2 selector, GPU-SKU registry, telemetry, and deterministic tests behind runtime flag

3) Perf characterization + regression hardening
- Expand benchmark matrix; run on A100/H100/L40S; tune thresholds for long-context tail latency
- Microbench overhead limits: selector eval + telemetry within agreed CPU budget

4) Staged canary rollout
- Hosted: start 1% traffic for allowlisted models/regions, then 5%/25%/50%
- Dedicated: enable per-pool (opt-in), then expand to default for validated SKUs
- Rapid rollback: disable v2 by model/GPU/region; pin kernel via override; denylist updates hot-reload

5) GA
- Default-on for Hosted for allowlisted models; Dedicated enablement per pool/SKU; publish release notes and runbooks

Top risks / mitigations
- Risk: long-context misclassification causing tail spikes
  Mitigation: conservative thresholds; explicit long-context bucket; denylist + rapid rollback; PR #28522
- Risk: non-deterministic selection due to time-varying inputs / floating comparisons
  Mitigation: determinism standard + replay tests; stable feature hashing; bounded candidate sets
- Risk: telemetry cardinality + ingestion load
  Mitigation: sampling policy; limited candidate logging; dashboard query review with Observability
- Risk: GPU SKU naming ambiguity across clouds / MIG
  Mitigation: normalization layer; explicit SKU mapping; fail-closed to safe fallback kernels
